This ultimate length is attained through a prolonged growth phase following the onset of gonadal maturation, which occurs at a total length of 38.8 cm [Lp = 38.8 cm], a size threshold that marks the transition from the juvenile to the adult stage. Broader ecological studies of haemulids suggest this strategy buffers against the high natural mortality typical of pelagic larval stages. The combination of a long lifespan and a high daily reproductive rate is consistent with a strategy for population persistence in variable tropical reef environments.

Reproductive investment in Diagramma pictum is tightly linked to body size, as the daily rate increases markedly once females surpass the size at puberty.
